title: Who & What is the Abomination of Desolation

sense.text: “Why speakest thou unto them in parables?” A parable is an illustrated story. Another word for that is allegory, another word for that is similitude, another word for that is proverb. That’s what the disciples asked: why do you speak to the people in illustrated stories, in allegories and metaphors and similitudes? Why don’t you talk plainly?

“Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven”: the Lord gave the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven to the disciples. He didn’t teach all Israel plainly, but he spoke to the disciples plainly. Why? Because they are the teachers, they are the instructors, they are the guiders.

“But to them it is not given”: to the rest of Israel. Why wasn’t it given unto them? Because of order. There had to be order: there are teachers and there are disciples, and disciples means students. Everybody’s not the teacher.

And the Lord knows how our people are. As soon as you create an organization amongst black people, what does every black person want to do? Be the HNIC. That’s why Christ said no, I’m not telling all of them plainly, I’m only telling y’all, because y’all the teachers. I’m setting you up as the guidance, as the instructors, as the leaders.

precepts.why:
Jump down in the same chapter: “All these things spake Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them”. Without an illustrated story he spake not unto them, not unto the multitudes of Israel.

“That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.” Things kept secret from the foundation of the world, meaning from the time of Genesis. The multitude got the parables; the mysteries were given to the teachers.

“But he that giveth his mind to the law of the most High”: that’s what most people miss. When I came in the truth in 1990, what we wanted to hear was prophecies; we wanted to hear the white man is the devil and the intricacies of the scriptures. But when it came to the law, the law classes were empty. Teach the prophecies and the crowd would come around; teach the law and you see everybody leave. Nobody wanted to hear that.

“And is occupied in the meditation thereof”, of God’s law, “will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.” See it as a step to understanding the prophecies, and to get the better understanding. That’s why the first thing is the law of the Most High, followed by seeking out the wisdom of all the ancient, and being occupied in prophecies. That’s the order of understanding.

That’s what a lot of Israelites miss, and this is why you hear strange doctrines out there about raping women, about polygyny, having a group of women. Listen to this: when we were in our homeland and we governed and ruled ourselves under the Most High and had wealth, then we had more than one wife. But you won’t find one scripture from the time of the Assyrian captivity on of Israel in captivity in another land having a group of women as their wives. You won’t read it in the Bible. You working in McDonald’s, you working in Home Depot with a group of women, and the women is the one making the money, taking care of his rusty black behind? Selling oils on the oil table? You’ve got to be kidding me. And if you fell for that, shame on you. Don’t come running over here, being wife number three, talking about now I want to get my life right. We’ve been warning for years; you saw us on the street teaching and you gave us the finger. Now he kicked you to the curb and got another wife number three, and you mad now. Well, shame on you, sister.

“He will keep the sayings of the renowned men: and where subtil parables are, he will be there also.” Why? Because he learned God’s law. He understood the law, and now he says, now I’m ready to get into these parables; now I can understand, because I understand the law.

“He will seek out the secrets of grave sentences, and be conversant in dark parables.” That’s why, when I get around the Bishops, the deacons and the captains, that’s what we talk about: the grave sentences and dark parables. That’s why it says how beautiful it is for brethren to dwell together in unity, and iron sharpeneth iron.

sense.text:
Just the other day our brother Jason Whitlock had an interview and accused me and the rest of the Israelites of racial idolatry. He claimed we worship our complexion and that our complexion is what will save us. We’ve never taught that at all, and this verse proves it’s not about our complexion.

“I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom”. Egypt was a Nilotic, Hamitic, black-skinned race just like us; they look very similar except for the phenotypes. They were black-skinned as well, and God said I gave them for your ransom. When you ransom something you give them up; you destroy them.

“Ethiopia and Seba for thee”: he gave up Ethiopia and Seba for us. So he got rid of three black nations to redeem us from slavery. God destroyed three black nations to save another black and brown nation, the nation of Israel. It has nothing to do with our complexion. It has everything to do with our lineage, our ancestry, our seed.

Now, in brief, true racial idolatry. “And it was given unto him”: the him is the skull, the so-called white man. Write this down: it started with Rome, Spain and Portugal. Rome gave the order; Portugal and Spain carried it out. They were the first ones.

“To make war with the saints”: they made war with us. Spain and Portugal made war with us, followed by the Dutch, followed by the English. “And to overcome them”: they conquered us and enslaved us.

“And power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.” Not only did they conquer the Israelites; when they came in power as Britain, Britain took over everything. They took over India, they took over China, they took over Japan. That’s why in those movies set in the Boxer Rebellion they’re always fighting against the British to get them out of the land.

“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him”: you got to emphasize him. It ain’t saying worship everybody on the planet; it’s talking about a specific race that he’s calling him. This is your Caucasian: Rome, Spain, Portugal, the Dutch, which is the Netherlands, Amsterdam, the English, the British, America. This is the him, “whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.”

This is racial idolatry: when you got black nations worshiping Caucasians. Look at the images: black people kissing images of the so-called holy, other nations kissing the white man as Jesus. You can’t make this stuff up. And it gets worse: Kirk Franklin, the gospel singer of the ages, kissing the hand of Billy Graham, the dirty white man. Look at the arrogance, like you better kiss my ring. People ask me what’s wrong with gospel music: gospel music is glorifying white supremacy. Christianity glorifies white supremacy and democracy. It has nothing to do with the love of our race, our people, nothing at all. It’s all about the glory of the white man, worshiping him. The white man ain’t even got to wash his hands when he used the bathroom.

This is what Christianity has done to our people. The brother on the left: there was nothing wrong with his skin, but Christianity taught him to despise himself so much he went and got cream to change his image, and his lips too. You look like a zombie. Why idolatry? Because he wants to look like him. There was nothing wrong with Sammy Sosa on the left at all, but Christianity taught him to hate himself and to worship him, look like him, and he bleached and dyed his skin. A famous Haitian brother: nothing wrong with his complexion on the left, but Christianity taught him to worship him.

My brother Michael Jackson: nothing wrong with him on the left, nothing at all. But remember he was a devout Jehovah’s Witness, and Christianity taught him to worship him. He carved his nose, carved his face, changed his hair, his lips, his eyebrows, his eyelashes, everything. Nothing wrong with Lil Kim on the left, but now she looks like the Cheshire cat; they bleached the skin to worship. Serena Williams: the bleach don’t work on your knees, your elbows, your knuckles and the back of your neck. She changed her eyes, everything; she looks scary now, and she’s still got them strong hands. A Haitian sister: her hands don’t match her face. And she even got yellow hair, and Serena has yellow hair too. This is racial idolatry.

Write it down: Imitation of Life, an excellent movie, done in two versions. A black woman had a daughter that was able to pass for white. She passed off as white to date a white man, and when it came out, the white boy beat her silly. Her mother came to find her and she cursed her black mother out: if you see me, walk your black behind on the other side of the street, I don’t want nobody to know you’re my mother. precepts.why:
I need you to see what the Bible says about yellow hair. “If a man or woman have a plague upon the head or the beard; Then the priest shall see the plague: and, behold, if it be in sight deeper than the skin; and there be in it a yellow thin hair; then the priest shall pronounce him unclean”. If the priest found a yellow thin hair, you’re unclean. “It is a dry scall, even a leprosy upon the head or beard.” That’s leprosy.

We’ve never been taught that in Sunday school, never been taught that in church. So our sisters dyed their hair yellow, and it’s not just the sisters; I’ve seen brothers dye their hair yellow too. Some of our people are born with yellow hair; it’s still unclean hair, but they were born like that. Not you trying to push that image. That’s unclean; that’s a leprosy of the hair.

I want everybody to hear: the Bible says “Envy thou not the oppressor”. When you envy the oppressor you want to look like him, you want to be him, you want to walk like him, you want to talk like him, just like him or her.

“And choose none of his ways”: you want his religions, you want his politics, you want his holidays, you want his woman, you want his man, her man. You want to be them. The Bible says choose none of his ways.

“Not setting by the honours of their fathers”: the Israelites did not set by the honours of their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Joshua, Malachi, Ezekiel, Christ. “But liking the glory of the Grecians best of all”: we liked the glory of the Grecians, the white man, best of all. What is this describing? Racial idolatry. We wanted to be like the white man.

“By reason whereof sore calamity came upon them”: because we worship him, sore calamity came upon us as a people. “For they had them to be their enemies and avengers”: the white man was always our enemies and avengers. “Whose custom they followed so earnestly”: we follow their customs so earnestly. “And unto whom they desired to be like in all things”: we desire to be like the white man in all things. What do you eat, how do you dress, how do you wear your hair, what gods do you worship, what political systems do you have? We wanted to be like him in all things: assimilation. Racial idolatry.

We didn’t want to even keep God’s holidays; instead we wanted to celebrate Caucasian holidays of oppression. Memorial Day is in celebration of all the wars the white man won. The Fourth of July is in honor of their independence from Britain, the war of independence; it has nothing to do with us. Thanksgiving was their destruction of Reuben and Issachar, the destruction of the American Indians, the indigenous Indians, the destruction of our brothers, and we wanted to celebrate that. Then you got lying Christians saying oh no, it’s just about giving God thanks for the good things in your life. Stop your lies. I always hear black women say that. Why I gotta be on that day, at that moment, with that course of food the white man says? You’re a black liar, stop your lies.

Then you got Christmas: that’s a holiday of our destruction as well. They gave gifts one to another on Christmas Day, stemming from the time of Nimrod on up. And in church, oh it’s for the children, oh it’s the birth of Jesus. What scripture is that? It’s not in the Bible. These are days of oppression we celebrate.

“And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee”: the Lord prophesied that the Israelites would discontinue from the heritage he gave us. Discontinued from our identity, our nationality; we wouldn’t know our country, our language, our culture. We would lose it all. “And I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not”: that’s where we’re living now, serving our enemies in a land.

Put it on the screen: in the Netherlands and Amsterdam, Black Pete was the servant to Saint Nick, Santa Claus. In America they don’t deal with Black Pete, they call it the elves, but this is what it represented: the elves represent black people, Santa Claus’s slaves. This was Santa Claus, Saint Nick, and his slaves, from when they conquered the Moors in Spain and Portugal, and this was their Christmas celebration: white people with blackface on, mocking us all over Europe. Here in America they use elves to hide it more cleverly. They don’t want Judah to wake up over here; they said if we use Black Pete over here, dumb Negroes just might wake up. He got fringes on the blue: they know exactly what they’re doing.

“For ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

sense.text: We’re going to deal with the holiday the Lord gave us, called the Feast of Dedication; in Hebrew it is called Hanukkah, which means feast of dedication. “And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter”: it’s a winter holiday.

“And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon’s porch.” Jesus observed it: he went into the temple because they were celebrating the Feast of Dedication.

You can read about the Feast of Dedication in brief in Daniel chapter 11, but in fullness you can read about it in First Maccabees chapter 4. That’s why, when Christians say the Apocrypha is not canon, disregard everything they say.

“When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)”. Christ said when you see the abomination of desolation that Daniel spoke of stand in the holy place, let him that readeth understand. Why would he say that? Because Daniel prophesied about the abomination of desolation twice. He prophesied of it during the time of the Greeks, and that’s what we read about now.

“Yea, he magnified himself even to the prince of the host”: this is Antiochus Epiphanes the Fourth. “And by him the daily sacrifice was taken away”: he made a law forbidding the Israelites to sacrifice the lambs or the goats or the oxen to the Lord of heaven and earth. “And the place of his sanctuary was cast down”: he cast down the sanctuary.

“And an host was given him against the daily sacrifice by reason of transgression”: write this down, the host that was given to him against the daily sacrifice was a group of Israelites that hated their own people.

“And it cast down the truth to the ground”: it cast down the truth of God to the ground. They despised it; the Greeks did not want to hear the scriptures. “And it practised, and prospered.”

“How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot?” In Daniel’s time it hadn’t occurred yet. Remember Daniel was in the Babylonian captivity; he’s prophesying two captivities later, because after Babylon came Persia and Media, then came the Greek captivity. So Daniel was prophesying centuries ahead.

“Unto two thousand and three hundred days”: two thousand three hundred days equals about six years and four months. That isn’t the time from Daniel to then; it’s the time period during it that this makes reference to. “Then shall the sanctuary be cleansed.”

precepts.why: I just got to prove it: “Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion”. That’s the host given him against the daily sacrifice. You had Israelites, just like we got today, who maintain their love of the white man, who maintain racial idolatry.

Go back to when they burned up the scriptures. “And when they had rent in pieces the books of the law which they found, they burnt them with fire.” That is how it cast down the truth to the ground.

“And whosoever was found with any the book of the testament”, “the king’s commandment was, that they should put him to death.” Do y’all see the hell and agony we went through? Not only did they burn up the scriptures, they killed us if they found us with the scriptures. In slavery, if they found us reading, they did that same thing; make no doubt about it. This is the same race of people over us, I don’t care how good they treat you on your job.

It says then shall the sanctuary be cleansed: “Then Judas appointed certain men to fight against those that were in the fortress, until he had cleansed the sanctuary.”

“So he chose priests of blameless conversation, such as had pleasure in the law”. See the warriors he chose. He couldn’t get just anybody to go do this thing; he said I need priests of blameless conversation who have pleasure in the law. That’s the type of brothers I like around me: brothers of blameless conversation that got pleasure in the law. When brothers come around we’ll be talking about scriptures, and then brothers be on that phone looking for stats of football players. Get the hell away from me, go over there and sit down somewhere; you ain’t ready for this, little boy. Sitting around thinking about some woman with a big behind, go sit down somewhere. I need men around me who love the law of the Most High. Those are the warriors; that’s who God is dealing with. The rest of you with your comic books, he ain’t dealing with you yet.

A sister wrote, make me believe I’m the only woman on the earth to you. Kick her to the curb: that’s a broken spirit, she ain’t ready for marriage. She wants to be an idol to him. Brother, you better find you a revolutionary woman who understands the Bible, who says you better go out there and fight for our people, fight for the laws of God. Any other kind of woman, don’t waste your time on her; she ain’t ready for this. And be careful, because some sisters lie till you get married: I’ll be the revolution and I’ll be exactly what you want until I get you.

Back to First Maccabees 4:41 again: we want to find out who the real soldiers are. Priests of blameless conversation such as had pleasure in the law: those are the soldiers, the warriors the Lord is looking for. I hope y’all men understand that. “Who cleansed the sanctuary, and bare out the defiled stones into an unclean place.”

“The altar of burnt offerings, which was profaned”: it was profaned because they sacrificed swine, pig, on the altar, and they put up the idol of Jupiter Olympus. “They thought it best to pull it down, lest it should be a reproach to them, because the heathen had defiled it”, “And laid up the stones in the mountain of the temple in a convenient place, until there should come a prophet to shew what should be done with them.” There were no prophets at that time: the intertestamental period, as the scholars call it, the time when there were no prophets.

“Then they took whole stones according to the law”: and as great as Judah Maccabee was, he never said I have a hundred percent truth. Be mindful of men that say they know everything; head for the hills when you hear men speak like that. They can’t even get out of the ghetto, but they know everything. “And built a new altar according to the former”: in order to build a new altar you had to know the law; you had to know the height and width of the altar. “And made up the sanctuary, and the things that were within the temple, and hallowed the courts.”

“They made also new holy vessels, and into the temple they brought the candlestick”: the candlestick is the seven-branch menorah, like the two we have up here, and all of them should be lit. Our custom is never to light one each day; we light the whole thing at once. “And upon the altar they burned incense, and the lamps that were upon the candlestick they lighted, that they might give light in the temple.” The lamps that were upon the candlestick: that’s all seven. They lit all seven; they didn’t light one one day and one the next day. “Furthermore they set the loaves upon the table, and spread out the veils, and finished all the works which they had begun to make.”

“Now on the five and twentieth day of the ninth month, which is called the month Casleu, in the hundred forty and eighth year”: the five and twentieth day is the 25th, and Casleu is the ninth month, which we call today November; when you start at March you got March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November. “They rose up betimes in the morning, And offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings, which they had made.”

“Look, at what time and what day the heathen had profaned it, even in that was it dedicated with songs, and citherns, and harps, and cymbals.” The same day that they defiled the temple was the same date, years later, that we dedicated it: the 25th of the ninth month. With songs and citherns and harps and cymbals we rejoiced; we partied.

“Then all the people fell upon their faces, worshipping and praising the God of heaven, who had given them good success.” I always pray for the good success of the nation of Israel. We want good success, so we got to pray to God Almighty, whose name is Yahuwah. You must pray.

“And so they kept the dedication of the altar eight days”: eight days, not seven days, eight days, “and offered burnt offerings with gladness, and sacrificed the sacrifice of deliverance and praise.”

sense.text:
“And arms shall stand on his part”: on the white man’s part. “And they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength”: Daniel is prophesying about the defiling of the temple by the Greeks.

precepts.why:

And they “brought in things that were not lawful”, like pig. “The altar also was filled with profane things, which the law forbiddeth”: pig.

“Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days”, nor the ancient feasts, “or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.” So don’t think it’s impossible for the United States of America to do the same thing. Of course they call it hate speech, anti-Semitism.

Don’t be online, especially you women who are all over the place teaching dumb narratives, wrong narratives.

They were the first nation to take the Bible and use it for their own agenda; just like the Greeks did, they put their images in it, and twisted scripture after scripture, just like they’re doing today: God loves everybody. The original Japheth was black skin, your Hawaiians, Samoans, those types of people; Japheth means good looking. Those were the original Greeks, the original black people of Greece.

They hold the dominion over all Europe: Esau, Idumea, Edom holds the dominion over all Europe. And Esau is detaining in captivity his brother Jacob, that’s us in captivity, at least as far as regards the tribe of Judah, till his Messiah, the Son of David, shall appear. There you go: until Christ.

sense.text:
“From David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations”. Write this down, this is what happened within those fourteen generations. The nation of Israel was split into two kingdoms, the Southern Kingdom and the Northern Kingdom: the Southern Kingdom led by Judah, the Northern Kingdom led by Ephraim. After that came the Assyrian captivity: they conquered the Northern Kingdom and took them into another land. After that came Babylon. Babylon not only took over Assyria and the Northern Kingdom, they conquered Judah, the Southern Kingdom, as well and made us slaves. Babylon were ancient Kush, Ethiopia. Write that down.

“And from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations.” From Babylon the Persian Mede captivity came about, then the Greek captivity, and then Christ was born during the Roman captivity. In case you don’t understand: Christ was born when Rome was ruling.

precepts.why:
This proves Christ was born when Rome was ruling: “there went out a decree from Cesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed.” Caesar Augustus was the second after Julius Caesar, his nephew, the second ruler. He was also known as Octavian: Augustus Octavian Caesar.

Write this down: when you read 2 Esdras chapter 11 and chapter 12, the second feather is Augustus Caesar. The first is Julius Caesar.
“For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.” So Christ was born during the time of Augustus, when Rome was ruling.

sense.text: His disciples came “for to shew him the buildings of the temple”. The temple was so beautiful. When you read the book of Haggai chapter 1 it didn’t look that good, but Herod made additions to the temple and made it more splendid to behold.
“There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.” Christ said there shall not be one stone left that is not thrown down.

precepts.why:
“When he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it, Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.” This is Christ prophesying. “Thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee”: Rome would cast a trench around Jerusalem. “And compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side”: Rome would circle and compass Jerusalem round and keep the Israelites in on every side. “And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another”.

Notice that in both of these Christ said there shall not be one stone standing. So what is that Wailing Wall that we always see? The book The Temples That Jerusalem Forgot shows Christ’s prophecies were accurate to a T: when the Romans got through with their fury dismantling Jerusalem and the temple, no stones were left in place that would make one believe there was once a city or a holy sanctuary there, and scholars cannot find any stone of the temple still in its original location. Its conclusion: the Wailing Wall was not a wall of the temple but is the western wall of Herod’s Fort Antonia. Herod built Fort Antonia next to the temple, and that is the wall still standing that everybody puts pieces of paper in and does a little stupid prayer. Fort Antonia is not the wall of the temple.

sense.text:
This explains what Christ was prophesying about. These curses take place over and over: it happened during the time of Babylon, it happened during the time of Greece and Rome, and here it is during Rome’s time.

“As swift as the eagle flieth”: the eagle was the symbol of Rome, this was their symbol, the eagle. “A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”: their language was Latin.

“A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old”: they didn’t care how old the Israelites were, “nor shew favour to the young”: they didn’t care about the babies of the Israelites.

“He shall eat the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy land, until thou be destroyed”, the “increase of thy kine”, meaning cattle, “or flocks of thy sheep”. Write this down: verse 51 describes colonialism. Not just Rome did it; it’s the same thing.
“He shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down”. That’s what we just read in Luke 19. The same thing Christ prophesied about is what Moses prophesied about.

“And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body”. Do y’all see that? Eat the fruit of your own body, meaning your children: “the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, which the Lord thy God hath given thee, in the siege, and in the straitness, wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee”.

“The man that is tender among you”: tender doesn’t mean homo. He was a prince; he wore the best clothes, ate the best food and lived in the best places, “and very delicate”. “His eye shall be evil toward his brother, and toward the wife of his bosom, and toward the remnant of his children”. Why would we have evil eyes toward our wife, our children and our brother? “So that he will not give to any of them of the flesh of his children whom he shall eat: because he hath nothing left him in the siege”.

We can only imagine how terrible a scene it must have been. The siege of Jerusalem that Rome did against us, think about it: no water went in or out, no food came into Jerusalem. Turn the water off and we’ll go crazy; we will devour each other, fight each other. No water, no food: how far would you go? Oh no, I’d never go that far, brother. The devil’s a liar.

“The tender and delicate woman among you, which would not adventure to set the sole of her foot upon the ground for delicateness and tenderness”: she had servants, and many times servants carried the woman, or they rode in carriages drawn by horses. “Her eye shall be evil toward the husband of her bosom, and toward her son, and toward her daughter, And toward her young one that cometh out from between her feet”. “For she shall eat them for want of all things”, and the want of all things in this case is food and water.

“Secretly”: imagine it. Y’all go to sleep, the baby is there, and in the middle of the night she wakes up or he wakes up, goes to the side of the corner, and covers the baby’s mouth so the baby can’t scream.

Why would this happen? “If thou wilt not observe to do all the words of this law that are written in this book”. Our people have a problem with God’s law. This is why things constantly go wrong for us, over and over and over. “That thou mayest fear this glorious and fearful name, THE LORD THY GOD”: in the Hebrew it says Yahuwah.

precepts.why:
This didn’t just happen during the time of Rome: “I will cause them to eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and they shall eat every one the flesh of his friend in the siege and straitness, wherewith their enemies, and they that seek their lives, shall straiten them.” That happened during the time of Babylon.

Now you may say to yourself, I would never do that. You don’t know what you’d do when you’re starving; you don’t know how far you’ll go when you’re starving.

sense.text:
Christ prophesied the same destruction of Jerusalem, and here is what he called the Romans. “When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet”: the white man is the abomination of desolation. Like a parable, today we call them code words, code words that only you and I know about. Other people say, what are you talking about, abomination? Christ knew and the disciples knew: the white man is the abomination of desolation.

“Stand in the holy place”: who is standing in the holy place? The white man, the Romans. They were the abomination of desolation; they are the abomination of desolation. Code words: write them down.

“Whoso readeth, let him understand”: because Daniel spoke of it twice, during the time of Greece and during the time of Rome, and Christ was in the time of Rome.

“But pray ye that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day”: because it would be a hard way to travel in the winter and on the sabbath day. The Romans knew they kept the sabbath day: we can get them on the sabbath day.

“In your patience possess ye your souls.” Why? Because we got to have patience to study, pray, apply. You don’t get it all in one day; it takes time, brothers and sisters. It takes patience to learn. That’s why they tell you to read four chapters a day: by the end of the year you have completed the entire Bible, and then you start again, because you’ll see things you didn’t see before. We’ve read the Bible many times and we’re still going over things saying, I never noticed that, I never saw that. It happens all the time.

“And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies”: Roman armies. “Then know that the desolation thereof is nigh. Then let them which are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out”. Christ told the disciples and the multitudes: when you see Rome start to come and encompass Jerusalem, run, run, run.

The wise, like the disciples, had already left and set things up in Egypt and different parts of Africa. They didn’t go up toward Assyria, because Rome had a foothold there. So we didn’t run that way; we ran towards Egypt and deep into the interiors.

Verse 22 is very important: “For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.” Written where? In Deuteronomy 28 that we just read. So what is Christ saying? Everything that’s written must be fulfilled. I can’t stop the prophecies.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: you Israelites. “And shall be led away captive into all nations”: you’re going to be made slaves in all nations. Who’s speaking? Christ.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: Jerusalem shall be taken over by the other nations, the white man in particular, “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”, until the Gentiles’ rulership is ended. What time period are we living in? The time of the Gentiles. The Gentiles are still ruling.

precepts.why:
Brothers that teach on the street, pay close attention: “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”.

Now Christians will say, why are we still in captivity if Christ redeemed us from those curses? Go back to Luke 21. Christ told us: “these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.” Everything that’s written must be fulfilled.

It precepts with this: “Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets”. Christ said I didn’t come to destroy the law, or anything the prophets said, like what Moses said; I didn’t come to change that. “I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.” He came to fulfill what is written about him being a sacrifice, but everything else must be fulfilled. That is why the days of vengeance still come.

sense.text:
The book From Babylon to Timbuktu: in the year 65 BC the Roman armies captured Jerusalem; in 70 AD General Vespasian and his son Titus put an end to the Jewish state with great slaughter; and in the time that followed it has been estimated that over one million Jews fled into Africa. precepts.why:
In case you don’t believe me: “what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine?” Tyre and Zidon were Canaanites, Nilotes, Hamites, and all the coasts of Palestine, those were the Palestinians. “Will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompense me, swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head”.

What did they do? They sold us into slavery. Tyre and Zidon and the Palestinians, the Arabs, sold us to the white man: “Because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things: The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians”. Who did it? The Nilotes, the Hamites. So you had the Africans, the Hamites, and the Arabs that sold us to the white man.

We’re reading Bible prophecy. This is primary source, written between two and three thousand years ago. This is the first and foremost book you go to.

sense.text: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity”: that is referring to Christ dying on the cross. “And to anoint the most Holy”: Christ is the most holy.

“Know therefore and understand”: Daniel says I want you to note this and understand this. “From the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem”: the commandment given by the Persians, from the time of Cyrus, “unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks”. We did classes on the seventy weeks; we went very slow and explained it in detail.

“And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: he shall die, but he did not die for himself. He died for the sins of the people.

“And the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”: the people of the prince that shall come is Rome. It wasn’t Israel; that’s Rome. “And unto the end of the war desolations are determined”: see that, it uses the term desolation for Rome too.

“And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week”: Rome made a covenant with the Israelites. One week breaks down to years, each day representing a year: seven years. “And in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”: just like Greece did, Rome did the same thing. I know I made a treaty with you, but I’m going to break it.

“And for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate”: Daniel is telling you Rome did the same thing Greece did. When you read about Greece it goes in detail: they put idols in the temple and throughout the cities of Judah, and they sacrificed swine’s flesh on the temple altar. Rome did the same thing.

Even Wikipedia, on Daniel’s prophecies about the abomination of desolation, says they seem to have at least a partial fulfillment in 167 BC, when a Greek ruler, Antiochus IV, desecrated the temple in Jerusalem. Antiochus called himself Epiphanes, which means god manifest. He set up an altar to Zeus, also called Jupiter, over the altar of burnt offering and sacrificed a pig on the altar; he slaughtered a great number of the Jews, sold others into slavery, forbade circumcision and required Jews to sacrifice to the pagan gods and eat pig. What we just read in Daniel about Rome, they patterned it after what the Greeks did.

But it was not a complete fulfillment: Antiochus Epiphanes did not enter a covenant with Israel for seven years. It was Rome that made the covenant. And in Matthew 24 Jesus, speaking some 200 years after Antiochus’s evil actions, spoke of Daniel’s prophecy as having a still future fulfillment: he was talking about Rome. We’re not waiting; it happened. The preterist view is that Jesus’s warning in Matthew 24:15 concerned the events leading up to the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70. And the writers know the same thing: what Greece and Rome did, they’re going to do similar things in these last days.

Christ prophesied under the Romans, not the Greeks. Here is Titus, a Roman with the eagle on his helmet, reigning 79 to 81 AD, one of the twelve feathers you read about in 2 Esdras 11 and 12. The twelve Caesars are your twelve feathers: it started with Julius Caesar, when Esau took over Rome, then Augustus, Tiberius, Caligula, Claudius, Nero, and on through Vespasian, Titus and Domitian, the twelfth. Vespasian was the governor in 70 AD and his son Titus was the general of the army; after Vespasian came his son Titus as the emperor, then Domitian, the Flavian emperors from 69 to 96 AD.

Then the siege, the fall of Jerusalem: when ye see Jerusalem compassed with armies, know that the desolation thereof is nigh. And this is when they robbed us and took our silver and gold: the Romans carrying out the menorah.
A parable of Rome. “The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son”: this is talking about the father and the son, and the son is Christ, Yahweh Shai.
“And sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the wedding: and they would not come.” Israel would not come.

“Again, he sent forth other servants”: these are the prophets that kept going out prophesying. “But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise: And the remnant took his servants, and entreated them spitefully, and slew them.” Israel hated the prophets; they slew them, they killed them.

When you read in Acts there was a manhunt for Peter. Peter was a fugitive, he was on the run, his wife was on the run; they were trying to kill them, and they did. John was exiled on the island of Patmos, and James was killed in Acts chapter 12: James was killed, Peter got arrested, then Peter got let out and he was on the run.

“But when the king heard thereof, he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city.” Those armies were Rome. They burned up Jerusalem. See what happened to Jerusalem: Christ prophesied what would happen for Israel stoning and killing the prophets.

“For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land, saith the Lord”: the Lord ain’t gonna pity us no more. “I will deliver the men every one into his neighbour’s hand, and into the hand of his king”. Who’s the king? He’ll deliver the Israelites into the hand of his king, Caesar. “And they shall smite the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them”: Rome, Caesar, will smite the land, and out of their hand the Lord will not deliver us.

“And I will feed the flock of slaughter, even you, O poor of the flock. And I took unto me two staves”: two sticks. A stave is a vertical wooden post or plank in a building or other structure, so it’s talking about pieces of wood, two pieces of wood. The two staves are the two kingdoms: the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Ephraim, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom.

“The one I called Beauty”: that’s Judah. “And the other I called Bands”: that’s the northern kingdom of Ephraim and the rest of them. “And I fed the flock”: that’s what we read in John 4. He fed the northern kingdom.

“Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; and my soul lothed them, and their soul also abhorred me.” These are the shepherds who hated the Lord, and the Lord hated them too. Those are the scribes, the Pharisees, the elders, the priests, all of them.

“Then said I, I will not feed you: that that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another.” What are they talking about? 70 A.D., the destruction of Jerusalem.

“And I took my staff, even Beauty, and cut it asunder”: he said, I’m gonna smite Judah, and that’s exactly what he did; he smote the southern kingdom. “That I might break my covenant which I had made with all the people.”

Remember the Lord was bringing the tribes together again, and we went to Acts 15 as verification for that.

“And it was broken in that day”: he broke the covenant between Judah and Ephraim again. Remember he was bringing them together; that’s what we read in John 4, and what you read about in Acts 10 and Acts 15. The Lord said, no, no, I’m gonna break it again.

“And so the poor of the flock that waited upon me knew that it was the word of the Lord.” The poor of the flock that waited upon Christ are the disciples and those that followed Christ, those that obeyed Christ. They didn’t wait for Rome to encircle Jerusalem; they was gone. Those disciples knew everything that Christ said was the word of the Lord, and they obeyed.

precepts.why:
Who’s the king Israel was delivered into the hand of? “Whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Cesar.” Pilate “saith unto the Jews, Behold your King!” “But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar.”

We have no king but Caesar. Our people loved Rome, and the chief priests loved Rome, because Rome gave them wealth, Rome gave them position, Rome gave them authority. So Christ’s crime was treason, for being king. That’s why Pilate kept mocking him, shall I crucify your king, and that’s what was on the cross. So when Zechariah says “into the hand of his king”, the king is Caesar.

This explains the three shepherds who hated the Lord. The Son of man must “be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes”: the elders, the chief priests and the scribes are your three, and you got your Pharisees and your Sadducees as well, all mixed up in them three.

This shows the two staves are the two kingdoms. “Take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions”: one stick, one stave. Judah and his companions were Benjamin and Levi.

“Then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions”: the other stick is the northern kingdom, Ephraim and his companions, which were Zebulon, Naphtali, Issachar, Gad, Reuben, Simeon and Asher.

“And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief”: this is referring to Judah. “Shall be graffed in”. A graft is a shoot or twig inserted into a slit on the trunk or stem of a living plant, from which it receives sap. You take one piece of plant and put it to another, and you graft them together, so that that twig lives and flourishes based on the one that’s rooted and grounded.

“For God is able to graff them in again”: meaning bring them back again. Notice the word again, because Christians on the street will try to pull this on you, that it’s talking about white people and other nations. Oh no. When was Esau grafted in? When were the Philistines with us, or the Moabites? Never. It’s talking about Israel.

“For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature”: this is the northern kingdom. We were wild by nature, disobedient. “And wert graffed contrary to nature into a good olive tree”: the Lord brought you, northern kingdom, back. “How much more shall these, which be the natural branches”: the kingdom of Judah, “be graffed into their own olive tree?”

Verse 26 explains the whole chapter: “And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob”. The whole chapter is talking about the Israelites. It’s not talking about Moabites being grafted in, or Canaanites being grafted in. Don’t let Christian stupidity fool you.

“Then saith the woman of Samaria unto him”, unto Christ, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Why? Because there was a split in the nation of Israel into two kingdoms.

“Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.” This is the flock he fed in Zechariah 11:7.

Who are the Samaritans? “Within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people. And the head of Ephraim is Samaria”. The head of Ephraim is Samaria, so the woman of Samaria in John 4 is of Ephraim, the northern kingdom.

“The woman saith unto him, I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ: when he is come, he will tell us all things. Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he.” Christ told a woman in Samaria, I’m the Messiah, I’m the one you’ve been waiting for.

“And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him”. “They besought him that he would tarry with them: and he abode there two days.” Christ stayed with the Samaritans, Ephraim, for two days. “And know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world”: the savior of the world of Israel.

So Christ did bring in the northern kingdom, and that goes with Acts chapter 10. There’s a lot of confusion about that even today: you have some Israelite camps that teach the Samaritan woman was not an Israelite. Then why would Christ reveal himself to them, why would Christ stay with them two days? It makes no sense. That’s the “I fed the flock” of Zechariah 11:7.

“There shall not be a coal to warm at, nor fire to sit before it”: when you sit down before a fire, that’s the warmness to comfort yourself. There ain’t gonna be no comfort for Babylon, for America.

“Thus shall they be unto thee with whom thou hast laboured”: your companies, your allies. “Even thy merchants”: your companies. “They shall wander every one to his quarter; none shall save thee.” So brothers and sisters, never give up.

precepts.why: What are the rivers she passes over? “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”. The water is represented by the word; the word is represented as water.

“Behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward”. This also goes with Isaiah 2, the law shall go forth from Zion. “And, behold, there ran out waters on the right side”: remember the waters represent the word of God, the law.

“Again he measured a thousand, and brought me through; the waters were to the loins.” Now the water comes to the loins: more understanding. Those that succeed us, that come after us, if there’s another generation, are going to be judged on another level, because they were given more understanding: to whom much is given, much is required.

“Afterward he measured a thousand; and it was a river that I could not pass over: for the waters were risen, waters to swim in, a river that could not be passed over.” This water represents the word of God being taught and coming out: these are the rivers Babylon passes over in Isaiah 47:2.

How the word reveals the wicked. “For the mystery of iniquity doth already work”: the mystery of iniquity is a metaphor, just like the abomination of desolation is a metaphor. Why a mystery? Because when you tell people all the atrocities he’s done, and that Israelites are the ones he did it to, our people say, oh no, it could never be, I don’t believe it, that ain’t Jesus.

“Only he who now letteth will let”: God is letting them rule. The he there is the Lord Almighty, Yahuwah; he’s the one that lets them rule. “Until he be taken out of the way”: until the white man be taken out of the way.

“And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth”. The spirit of God’s mouth is the Bible. How is it revealing them?
